key_insight: Heating duration during electrocontact welding of a woven steel mesh to bronze can be predicted from pulse power and mesh geometry to identify when wire penetration into the base metal begins.
engineering_relevance: The model helps set welding pulse timing for consistent joint formation and deposited layer quality in mesh-to-bronze repair or surfacing operations.
method: Bronze BrOCC5-5-5 samples were prepared with lathe-machined surfaces (Rz ≈ 35 μm).
A low-carbon steel woven mesh (St1kp, square mesh) was welded using the 01.11-022 Remdetal setup.
Process variables included 5.0–6.0 kA current, 1.2 kN pressure, 0.02–0.1 s pulse duration, and 0.16 s inter-pulse time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports derived analytical formulas linking temperature rise, critical penetration onset, and welding time to pulse thermal power and mesh geometry, with deposited layer thickness around 0.30–0.35 mm.
watch_item: The abstract describes a theoretical model and process window, but it does not provide the full experimental validation metrics or error bounds for the predictions.
paper_title: The effect of heating duration on the strength of a joint obtained by electrocontact welding of a metal woven mesh to a bronze part
